result: Reviewed UniProtKB entries read on 2026-10-21 through rest.uniprot.org, annotation update 2026-09-02. CACNA1C (Q13936, entry version 255): pore-forming alpha-1C subunit of the voltage-gated calcium channel that gives rise to L-type calcium currents, required for normal contraction of smooth muscle cells in blood vessels and in the intestine and essential for normal blood pressure regulation through contraction of arterial smooth muscle cells; expressed in vascular smooth muscle; inhibited by dihydropyridines such as isradipine and by nifedipine; the channel complex contains one each of alpha, beta, gamma and delta subunits and is modulated by CACNB1, CACNB2, CACNB3, CACNA2D1 and CACNA2D4; activity is regulated by calcium and calmodulin, and phosphorylation by protein kinase A at Ser1981 activates the channel. The selectivity-filter motifs of the four repeats are TMEG at 361-364, TGED at 704-707, TFEG at 1133-1136 and TGEA at 1462-1465, each containing one glutamate, and Glu363, Glu1135 and Glu1464 are annotated as sites of calcium ion selectivity and permeability; dihydropyridine-binding regions span residues 1109-1198 and 1478-1546, and the phenylalkylamine-binding region spans 1492-1534. CACNA1C variants cause Timothy syndrome, long QT syndrome 8 and, with Brugada syndrome 3, loss of ion selectivity: Gly406Arg causes a nearly complete loss of voltage-dependent channel inactivation, Ile1186Thr shifts the voltage dependence of activation to a more negative potential with increased window and steady-state current, and Glu1135Lys, in the repeat III selectivity filter, causes loss of selectivity for calcium and other divalent cations over monovalent cations with increased sodium-mediated inward and potassium-mediated outward currents. CALM1 (P0DP23, version 62): calcium binding activates calmodulin, which stimulates myosin light-chain kinases among other enzymes, and mediates calcium-dependent inactivation of CACNA1C. MYLK (Q15746, version 244): calcium/calmodulin-dependent myosin light chain kinase that phosphorylates myosin light chains (EC 2.7.11.18) with Mg2+ and Ca2+ as cofactors; all catalytically active isoforms require binding to calcium and calmodulin for activation; variants cause familial thoracic aortic aneurysm 7, some of them decreasing kinase activity or calmodulin affinity, and megacystis-microcolon-intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome, a visceral myopathy with loss of smooth muscle contraction in the bladder and intestine. MYL9 (P24844, version 211): myosin regulatory light polypeptide 9 of smooth muscle; phosphorylation by MLCK/MYLK increases the actin-activated myosin ATPase activity and thereby regulates contractile activity; the 172-residue entry sequence begins with the initiator methionine and carries phosphothreonine at position 19 and phosphoserine at position 20, the residues numbered Thr18 and Ser19 when the initiator methionine is excluded. PPP1CB (P62140, version 213): protein phosphatase 1 beta catalytic subunit, which hydrolyses O-phospho-L-seryl-[myosin light chain] and O-phospho-L-threonyl-[myosin light chain] (EC 3.1.3.53) with Mn2+ as cofactor; PPP1R12A, PPP1R12B and PPP1R12C mediate its binding to myosin. PPP1R12A (O14974, version 223): protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 12A, also called MYPT1, a key regulator of protein phosphatase 1C that mediates binding to myosin. CYP3A4 (P08684, version 254): a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase that metabolises the majority of administered drugs, inserting one oxygen atom into a substrate with two electrons provided by NADPH through cytochrome P450 reductase, and induced by drugs such as rifampicin.
